combo_tournament_winners#cb_environment_.rationale: The review record does attach ten.venue_speed_history and ten.wind_indoor to the environment category (the first pass wrongly said neither is attached) and ten.joint_event_correlation carries the shared shock between legs. What is open is an unverified per-event pace index and a weather archive keyed to match times (source problem; Open-Meteo hourly archive is a free candidate), plus the size of the cross-tour dependence, which is empirical.

game_winner_inplay#gw_listing_time.rationale: The existence layer is already authored (stage s7: P(set M played and reaches game N) from ten.games_per_set_distribution, ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge, ten.set_first_server_sequence, ten.format), so listing time changes no input; it only fixes how much existence mass remains at trade time. It needs market open_time from Kalshi market metadata joined to match/set start times, which the rules sample lacks.

match_winner#mw_doubles_format.rationale: Verified: ATP/WTA tour (and Challenger) doubles use no-ad scoring with a 10-point match tiebreak in place of the third set (since 2005 on ATP); Slam doubles use full sets with a 10-point tiebreak at 6-6 in the final set. ten.format is already defined as a per-event-year lookup (sets, final-set rule, tiebreak, no-ad), so this changes no input; what remains is compiling the per-event values from rulebooks and tournament pages.

match_winner#mw_misfiled_series.rationale: Records defect: eight tournament-named round-winner series (KXATPAMT, KXATPMC, KXATPMIA, KXATPMAD, KXWTAIWO, KXWTAMIA, KXWTAMAD, KXWTADDF) are filed under match_winner while the mechanically identical KXATPIWO/KXATPIT/KXATPMCO series sit in tournament_winner_futures, so the same object gets two mechanisms. Exhibition format is already covered by ten.exhibition_format_effort, and the KXATPGAME/KXWTAGAME title-only question is contract-side (Kalshi wording).
match_winner#mw_misfiled_series.catalog_action: Re-file the eight round-winner series into tournament_winner_futures (path/round-reach mechanism, ten.path_difficulty_sim, walkover terms) with a cross-reference from match_winner, so both archetypes and the series ledger map one object to one archetype; leave KXATPGAME/KXWTAGAME as an UNVERIFIABLE_CONTRACT note.

player_aces_and_double_faults#ac_pair_co.rationale: The shared drivers of a match-total count are already inputs (ten.service_points_scenario_mixture for joint exposure, ten.wind_indoor/venue pace for environment, ten.ace_count_distribution for overdispersion); the open item is the size of the residual cross-player correlation after conditioning, a parameter estimable from Sackmann w_ace/l_ace/svpt. The review also notes no match-total ace or DF series is listed, so nothing currently depends on it.

retirement_walkover_participation#rp_led.rationale: Not a mapping defect: the archetype's mechanism already separates the chains into stages (s1-s4 participation/return survival, s5 retirement announcement hazard, s7 return from completed retirement) with dedicated inputs (ten.layoff_survival_curve, ten.retirement_announcement_hazard, ten.unretirement_reentry_status). Whether these warrant separate registry archetypes is an organisational choice that only matters if their calibration behaves differently, which data settles; no input is missing.

retirement_walkover_participation#rp_ree.rationale: Verified: WADA Code Art. 5.6.1 (mirrored in the ITIA TADP) requires a retired Registered Testing Pool athlete to give six months' written notice before returning to international competition (longer if residual ineligibility exceeds six months; WADA may grant an exemption). This matches the six months already in ten.unretirement_reentry_status, so the input list is unchanged; the remaining issue is that ITIA does not publish a public list of return notices.

season_ranking_and_majors#sr_finals_qual.rationale: The catalog measurement is demonstrably wrong: ten.remaining_race_arithmetic replaces a withdrawn qualifier with the next alternate, but the KXATPFINALSQUAL/KXWTAFINALSQUAL rules say Yes even if a qualified player does not compete. It also omits the verified ATP rule that a current-year Grand Slam champion finishing 8th-20th in the Race takes the 8th place instead of the 8th-ranked player, which adds a required input (current-year major winners) to the ATP race computation.
season_ranking_and_majors#sr_finals_qual.catalog_action: Rewrite ten.remaining_race_arithmetic for the Finals-qual series: P(Yes)=P(top-7, or 8th subject to the Grand Slam champion 8-20 rule) without a withdrawal reduction; add current-year major winners (ten.career_major_count_state) as an input for ATP; confirm the WTA rule, cut-off date and alternate settlement from the ATP/WTA rulebook chapters.

season_ranking_and_majors#sr_issuance_ti.rationale: Issuance is the market open time, which is Kalshi market metadata not present in the rules sample; ten.career_major_count_state already defines the state variable (major count with dates) the contract is checked against. Pulling open_time changes no input, it only fixes the anchor date for the count, so this is a missing data field rather than missing catalog content.

season_ranking_and_majors#sr_snapshot_so.rationale: ten.ranking_publication_calendar already encodes the rule (applicable list = latest publication <= settlement time). Whether ATP/WTA publish any list in December after the year-end ranking (released after the Finals in November) changes which date is looked up, not which inputs are required; I could not confirm the December schedule from search, and it is settled from dated ranking archives (Sackmann rankings files, ATP/WTA ranking pages).

season_ranking_and_majors#sr_wta_model.rationale: The inputs are defined (ten.major_winner_concentration, ten.major_participation_hazard); the gap is that their parameters have not been fitted separately for the WTA, and whether WTA parity and turnover warrant separate shrinkage is a calibration question settled with 10+ years of Slam data. Keying the parameters by tour is part of fitting, not a missing input or mechanism.

tournament_winner_futures#tw_round_robin.rationale: Verified from the official Nitto ATP Finals rules page and the ATP rulebook (Chapter IV): order is wins, matches played, head-to-head (two tied), then % sets won, % games won, ranking (three tied). This matches ten.round_robin_group_structure, and Next Gen short sets/no-ad are covered by ten.short_format_rules, so the input list is unchanged; what remains is ingesting per-year rulebook values for ATP, WTA and Next Gen.
